common_name: Party Line Blue Flag Iris (Red-Purple Native Iris Cultivar)
directions: Set divisions of the rhizome shallowly at the soil surface in consistently wet, humus-rich soil at a pond margin, bog garden, or rain garden, choosing a spot in full sun for the best bloom. This compact selection of the native blue flag iris stays under two feet tall and produces red-purple flowers with darker veining and a pale yellow signal that fades toward white as the bloom ages. Like the species, it tolerates shallow standing water and spreads gradually by rhizome to form a tidy, non-invasive clump. Divide congested clumps every three to four years in early spring or right after flowering to maintain vigor.

common_name: Whodunit Blue Flag Iris (White-Falls Native Iris Cultivar)
directions: Plant rhizome divisions with the top just at the soil surface in wet, acidic, humus-rich soil along a pond edge, streambank, or rain garden basin. This native selection bears violet-blue flowers boldly veined in purple over falls that are mostly white, giving strong visual contrast against the upright blue-green foliage. Grow it in full sun to light shade, keeping the soil saturated to a few inches of standing water through the growing season. Established clumps spread steadily by rhizome and benefit from division every four to five years to keep them vigorous.

common_name: Mysterious Monique Blue Flag Iris (Near-Black Purple Native Iris Cultivar)
directions: Grow this striking selection of blue flag iris in permanently moist to wet, humus-rich acidic soil at a pond margin or bog garden, in full sun to part shade. Registered in the 1980s, it produces midseason flowers with pale violet standards set above dramatically dark, almost black-violet falls marked with a bright white signal patch. Plant rhizome divisions shallowly, with the top of the rhizome at or just below the soil surface, and keep the site consistently saturated. It is slower to bulk up than the wild species, so avoid dividing established clumps more often than every four to five years.

common_name: Between the Lines Blue Flag Iris (Variegated-Leaf Native Iris Cultivar)
directions: Plant rhizome divisions shallowly in wet to consistently moist, humus-rich soil at a pond margin, streambank, or bog garden, siting the clump in full sun to part shade. Grown primarily for its cream-and-green striped, sword-shaped foliage, this cultivar also produces the violet-blue, purple-veined flowers typical of the wild blue flag iris in late spring. The variegation shows most vividly in cooler weather and strong light, and tends to green up somewhat by midsummer. Divide clumps every four to five years in spring to refresh vigor and maintain crisp leaf striping.
